newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade slow,thin test-feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade slow,thin test-feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday Wednesday was slow, with not enough sales for an adequate market test, USDA and feedlot sources said.
About 500 heifers sold in Kansas at $66.50 per cwt, USDA said. The cattle weighed 1,225 pounds and will likely grade select to mostly choice, according to USDA.

The bulk of cattle were bid at $65.00 which was passed by owners pricing cattle mostly at $67.00, cattle feeders said. Owners were comfortable with light-weight cattle supplies and holding out for steady to higher prices, they said.
Feedlot cattle were running at weights well below a year ago because strong beef demand had feedlots this fall and winter pulling cattle ahead of schedule.

Last week's winter storm in the Plains also kept weights down by slowing gains during extremely cold weather. Cattle that did eat were converting feed to stay warm and were not putting on weight, sources said.
USDA estimated slaughter cattle weights the week ended January 18 at 1,154 lbs, down eight lbs from 1,162 lbs the previous week and 39 lbs below the actual average weight of 1,193 lbs a year ago.
